newsitem.title: UK: Zeneca says handful of asthma complications.
newsitem.headline: Zeneca says handful of asthma complications.

text.p: British pharmaceuticals company Zeneca Group Plc said on Thursday it had received reports of a "handful" of cases of complications involving patients taking its asthma drug Accolate.
A company spokesman told Reuters the problems were related to patients who had reduced their intake of oral steroid drugs at the same time as taking Accolate.
"Zeneca does not believe there is a causal relationship with Accolate," the spokesman said.
He denied reports that the drug, launched in the U.S. earlier this year, had led to some deaths.

"We have received reports that in very severe cases, the reduction in oral steroid dose in patients with Accolate has been followed by the onset of eosinophilic conditions and symptoms that go with that," which include respiratory and pulmonary problems and cardiac complications.
The spokesman said Accolate was being taken by between 250,000 and 300,000 patients in the U.S. alone. The drug is mainly targeted at patients with mild to moderate asthma.
Zeneca told Reuters company officials had held talks with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and had agreed on a change to the labelling for Accolate.
The new labelling recommends that patients "should be instructed not to reduce the dose or stop taking any other asthma medication unless instructed by a physician."
